runtime.comparison_scope: All Git-tracked files under vllm/ at the runtime base commit; does not cover non-vllm files, generated build artifacts, installed dependencies, or runtime environment.

patch_changes: Explicitly set VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN for the isolated service.
Require all 32 diagnostic requests to return valid completions with nonzero output tokens.
Require all 16 warmup requests to return valid completions with nonzero output tokens.
Check service startup log for the FLASH_ATTN backend selection.

workload.arrival_pattern: Closed-loop concurrency-limited workload. All 512 futures are submitted to a ThreadPoolExecutor; up to 16 workers execute HTTP requests concurrently. Completed workers take queued requests. No fixed-rate or Poisson arrival pacing.

diagnostics.note: Diagnostic trace is separate from the three performance runs; detailed trace throughput is not used as the reported performance result.

provenance_notes: Runtime base commit and Runner bundle commit are distinct version identifiers.
The 1,779-file comparison establishes exact byte equality only for Git-tracked vllm/ files between the runtime base commit and the isolated source tree.
The complete experiment-time source fingerprint file was not uploaded; only its SHA-256 digest was recorded.
The local runner patch is identified by its SHA-256 digest; the full patch file was not available in the supplied output.
Arrival timing and server max_num_seqs are not recorded in run_config.txt and remain unverified here.
Performance results are observed benchmark results; fair comparison against native vLLM requires matching request arrival traces, concurrency, server settings, and model/runtime conditions.
The fingerprint contains 1,779 Git-tracked Runtime files and 7 additional FlashAttention build files copied into the isolated source tree.
The 7 additional files are build artifacts, not modifications to the 1,779 Git-tracked Runtime files.
The client submits all request futures to a 16-worker ThreadPoolExecutor; this is a closed-loop concurrency-limited workload, not an open-loop constant-rate or Poisson arrival process.
